waypoints.diagnosis: OPERATOR 2026-09-24 (via luthen-observability-9c): 'that's what happens if you don't promote per-core as part of the step building each core.' The make chain HAS a per-core promote target, yet the INSERT joined _ht_map over the WHOLE edge set — so each per-core promote evidently recomputes a GLOBAL height map. Fix = scope the height-map INSERT to the core being built (its own edges), inside that core's step, so cost is bounded per core and attributable to it. Backend 212335 is GONE (rolled back; no count fell). OPERATOR follow-up: 'the makefile had all of the promotion steps lined up … that makefile generator might have gotten trashed' — CHECKED 2026-09-24: the CURRENT agda/Flat.mk DOES line up per-core promotes (`$(BUILD)/%.promoted$(TSFX): %.ingested` → `sppf_db --promote-core <core>.agdai`); the committed HEAD Flat.mk has NO promote targets, and `git log --first-parent main -S promote-core/-S .promoted` finds nothing — the chain was never committed, its history is only in edit-snapshot refs (hundreds). So the per-core STEP exists; the table-wide `_ht_map` join is inside --promote-core's SQL (scripts/sppf_db.py). Candidates, only EXPLAIN can separate: (a) no/unused index on sandbox edge(core_id, plid) → every round seq-scans edge; (b) stale planner stats on the freshly-established sandbox tier (no ANALYZE on edge); (c) one core needing very many rounds. waypoints.evidence: backfilled from the ledger 2026-09-25. | 2026-10-02: 2026-10-02: landed the ledger-UNIT feature, ported from mtools' mikemol-membudget (commit 7196dc1 in their fence/), which built this first and recorded in its own commit message that bash's own status still said MB, which is substrate's to take up. Confirmed the safety precondition BEFORE writing anything (not assumed): gc's catch-all arm, release's grep -v ^LEASE, and _set_total's awk {print} pass-through all already preserve any non-LEASE/non-TOTAL_MB line verbatim, so a UNIT line is additive with zero risk to the existing format. Added: read_unit() in membudget-ledger (mirrors read_total's two-lines-refuses-exit-4 discipline); _set_unit()/_unit_operand() and init --unit WORD / init --reset N --unit WORD in membudget; cmd_status renders TOTAL/top-level-leased/global-free/per-lease amounts in the declared unit (MB renders byte-identical to before -- verified against the real production ledger, unchanged); cmd_run refuses (exit 4) before any lease when the ledger's unit isn't MB, since run caps HOST memory in MB and a non-MB lease would kill its own command. Verified end to end: a contexts ledger's run refuses correctly; an MB ledger's run/status/verify/verify-ceiling are all unaffected (full nested verify passed against the real 8192MB production ledger). shellcheck clean throughout. census: zero symlink adopters of scripts/membudget (confirmed 2 ticks ago), so no cross-repo compat risk. Staged scripts/membudget + scripts/membudget-ledger. | 2026-10-02: 2026-10-02: confirmed the third clause ('nest only under an own-ledger parent') is satisfied by construction, not left open. $FILE is derived identically on every invocation (${MEMBUDGET_FILE:-$HOME/.cache/membudget/budget.cotype}); a nested child inherits its parent's environment including MEMBUDGET_PARENT via export, and nothing in this script ever changes MEMBUDGET_FILE between a parent and the child it launches -- so a nested lease's $FILE is always the SAME ledger its parent's lease lives in, by the ordinary shell inheritance rule, with no extra mechanism needed. Traced the one way this could theoretically go wrong (a caller exporting a DIFFERENT MEMBUDGET_FILE for a nested child while still inheriting MEMBUDGET_PARENT from an unrelated outer lease): _parent_alive greps the CHILD's own $FILE for the parent id, finds nothing, and REFUSES loudly ('parent lease $parent is gone') rather than silently cross-referencing or double-counting -- a safe failure mode, and not a path any current caller takes. All three clauses of W42's title are now satisfied: UNIT line support, status prints the unit, nesting is own-ledger by construction. Marked done.

waypoints.title: scripts/membudget: honour WAIT-line FIFO admission (mtools W48 / amr-skills W51) -- bash client currently jumps the Python queue
waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-02: 2026-10-02 tick: checked mtools' fence/ git log for relevant landings since mtools' W48 letter. FOUND: mikemol-membudget (fence/src/mikemol/fence/membudget_cli.py, commit b91641e, 2026-09-23) -- a PYTHON console script replicating bash membudget's verbs/exit-codes over fence's admission, SHARING ONE LEDGER FILE with substrate's real bash scripts/membudget, cross-client tested (5 tests drive both clients on one ledger; fence suite 212 passed). Its own residue R1 says explicitly: 'run applies no memory cap the way bash's scope does, so it is NOT a drop-in replacement for bash run' -- so this does NOT retire scripts/membudget or substitute for the fix scoped here; substrate's bash client is still the one that needs WAIT-line support for real builds (which carry the memory cap). BUT it IS a ready-made cross-client test harness/reference (test_membudget_cli.py, 581 lines, 36 cases) to validate the bash WAIT-line patch against once written -- worth reusing rather than inventing a fresh cross-client fixture. Also notable: b91641e PREDATES the WAIT-line commits (2596184, a892cc2 are later in the log), so its cross-client arm never exercised WAIT-line cooperation -- confirming mtools' own W48 letter is still accurate that bash-side FIFO is untested and unimplemented. | 2026-10-02: 2026-10-02: LANDED the full 4-step WAIT-line FIFO patch (append/read/gate-on/remove), ported from mtools' mikemol.fence.admit module -- read its full source (queued, my_turn, enqueue/dequeue, claim's head re-check) to port the exact semantics rather than re-deriving them. membudget-ledger gained _wait_head() (oldest live ticket) and _dequeue_wait() (best-effort removal, same shape as release), plus gc's WAIT arm (liveness-only reaping, no cascade -- a waiter has no children). scripts/membudget's cmd_run gained: queued (top-level AND mb greater than 0, exact mirror of the exemptions for nested and zero-mb requests), a lock-free head-of-line check before the claim attempt, an authoritative re-check of the head under the same lock as the budget re-check (closing the race the lock-free check alone cannot), WAIT-line removal in the same critical section as the LEASE append (so no reader ever sees both-queued-and-holding or neither), enqueue-once-on-real-block, and exit-trap cleanup for the ticket mirroring the existing lease-release pattern. shellcheck clean throughout; verify-ceiling and verify (nested disjoint allocation) both still PASS unchanged -- the new code path is inert for non-queued (nested or zero-mb) requests. POSITIVE CONTROL, the test that matters: held 80 of 100MB; launched a 50MB request (blocks, enqueues) then immediately a 10MB request (FITS the free 20MB on its own). Confirmed via real timestamps: the 10MB request CORRECTLY BLOCKED (need 10MB, free 20MB, waiting) despite fitting, and was admitted about 1s AFTER the 50MB request released its hold on the FULL pool -- exactly the head-of-line defect this waypoint exists to fix. Ledger showed zero orphaned WAIT/LEASE lines after both completed (clean exit-trap cleanup). Could not construct a reliable live NOBLOCK-refusal cross-call test due to apparent per-Bash-tool-call process/PID namespace isolation (a background job's PID from one tool call was not visible via proc in a later call) -- the cleanup path itself is unchanged in structure from the existing, already-proven release-on-exit-trap pattern, just extended to also dequeue, so this is a reasoned rather than directly observed guarantee for that one arm specifically. | 2026-10-02: 2026-10-02 tick: attempted live cross-client (bash vs mikemol-membudget python) WAIT-line FIFO validation, 3 separate trials. Basic cross-client cooperation on the budget semaphore itself is confirmed working correctly in all trials: python's mikemol-membudget and bash's scripts/membudget both correctly waited for each other's LEASE lines and were admitted only once capacity actually freed (this is the pre-existing guarantee mtools' own test_membudget_cli.py already covers). COULD NOT construct the specific WAIT-line race (python enqueues first, bash arrives second and must queue behind it) in this environment: python's interpreter startup overhead consistently exceeded the available timing control between sequential/parallel tool calls, so bash's competing small request always reached the ledger and got admitted into free capacity before python had enqueued its own WAIT line in all 3 tries -- an environmental/tooling limitation, not a code defect. Verified by inspection instead: bash's _wait_head()/_lease_fields() parse a WAIT line structurally (by field position), with no dependence on which client wrote it, so cooperation is guaranteed by the SHARED TEXT FORMAT rather than by anything client-specific -- the same argument mtools' own admit.py docstring makes for its LEASE-line compatibility. A genuine controlled race needs a test harness that starts both processes with controlled timing (mtools' own test_membudget_cli.py, which already does exactly this via tmp_path + stub systemd-run) rather than live ad-hoc backgrounding. | 2026-10-02: 2026-10-02: operator ruling supersedes — bash membudget to be PURGED (git rm), not maintained as a bridge. Bridge commit attempt failed on pre-existing unrelated gate failures (stale LEAF_MARKER import in tests/test_agda_census_drain.py, stale Selftest.mk) unrelated to membudget; not forcing it through since the file is slated for deletion once mtools:W427/W428/W429 land parity. Leaving WAIT-line patch staged, uncommitted. | 2026-10-10: 2026-10-10 CORRECTION: an earlier note here says mikemol-membudget run applies no memory cap (R1). That described mtools commit b91641e. The installed client at 6c242bba caps with a cgroup-v2 sibling (positive control in W324). Do not rely on the old R1 reading.

waypoints.title: Merge store_endpoint.resolve and vmagent_address.resolve into one luthen resolver caller with a runner seam
waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-10: 2026-10-10 MEASURED from the two modules. Same capability, two copies: vmagent_address.resolve(port, luthen) runs python -m checks.endpoints_query --side host NAME with cwd=luthen; store_endpoint.resolve() runs INTERPRETER RESOLVER postgres --side host by script path from module constants LUTHEN/RESOLVER/INTERPRETER (a second hard-wired checkout location, plus DEFAULT_LUTHEN in vmagent_address: THREE spellings of where luthen lives). Both parse one JSON line, require state answered with host (str) and port (int), refuse otherwise, and never fall back to loopback; store_endpoint also reads as_of. Exit codes per the resolver: 1 refused query, 2 unreadable declaration. Different refusal types (UnresolvedError vs EndpointError family) and different timeouts (10s vs 60s). Third consumer: vlogs_destination.destination() via vmagent_address.resolve. THE DESIGN: one clean module substrate/luthen_resolver.py exposing resolve(name) -> Answer(host, port, as_of) over an injected runner (the seam both suites already use), one argv builder (the only place that names where luthen lives), one refusal hierarchy that the two existing exception types subclass so callers do not change. store_endpoint and vmagent_address become thin adapters. | 2026-10-10: 2026-10-10 MEASURED importers with substrate.module_importers (plain pycodemod --importers returned 0 under both spellings, a fact about the spelling): vmagent_address <- build_active, prom_push, vlogs_destination, vlogs_destination_selftest (4); store_endpoint <- live_target, sandbox_target, sandbox_target_selftest, store_endpoint_selftest, store_launch, store_launch_selftest (6); 13 dynamic-import shapes the reader cannot resolve, none known to touch these. Reuse-index has no resolver module. Dispatched ONE write agent (a single sequential writer, per the standing rule) to create substrate/luthen_resolver.py plus its selftest and turn the two modules into thin adapters keeping every public name and making the old exceptions subclass the new ones. Runtime behavior must not change (by-path argv kept byte for byte). Not committed: W314. | 2026-10-10: 2026-10-10 DONE and independently verified. Created substrate/luthen_resolver.py (one argv builder, record_of, resolve(name, runner, luthen) -> Answer, ResolverError/NoAnswerError/UnusableAnswerError) and its selftest. vmagent_address and store_endpoint are thin adapters; old exceptions subclass the new ones. waypoints.title: Pin the luthen resolver reply contract as shared fixture cases and hand them to luthen as the client's acceptance suite
waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-10: 2026-10-10 DESIGN. The contract luthen's thin client must honour, as data: (1) answered: exit 0, one JSON line, state answered, host str, port int, as_of str. (2) refused query: exit 1, state not answered (name the state). (3) unreadable declaration: exit 2. (4) garbage or empty stdout: consumer treats as unresolved, never guesses. (5) unknown name: a non-answered state. (6) NO fallback to loopback in any case. Four consumer-visible fields only: state, host, port, as_of. These become the shared case table the merged luthen_resolver suite (W319) runs, and the same table goes to luthen as the acceptance fixture for their client, so 'the client works' is a thing both repos run, not a claim. The existing fixture-pair practice (mtools letters) is the precedent: one input, two expected outputs. | 2026-10-10: 2026-10-10 DONE. The 12 reply-contract rows are now DATA in substrate/luthen_resolver_cases.py (Case dataclass, CASES tuple, row(), main() exports JSON via python -m substrate.luthen_resolver_cases); luthen_resolver_selftest runs the table plus substrate's one argv case: 13/13 (re-run). Both files passed the strict per-file gate after two refusals I fixed (a long line, and asdict returning dict[str, Any], so rows are built field by field). A JSON file read from __file__ was rejected on purpose: it breaks the no-file-relative-paths rule and would not be packaged; a data module is importable, typed and packaged. Sent luthen the contract and how to use it as the acceptance suite as a letter: luthen-observability/inbox/2026-10-10-substrate-resolver-acceptance-cases.md (the producer-side reading: answered, refused exit 1, unreadable exit 2, never loopback; plus the images.json and default-root facts). COMPILE CHAIN: Flat.mk recipe (agda +RTS -M MEM_CAP, log redirect, separate touch) <- agda/Makefile:9-12 puts scripts/agda-shim first on PATH <- shim sets MEMBUDGET_RETRY_OOM=1, AGDA_MB auto, adds --profile=all and +RTS -s, parses profile to .agda-profile.tsv, strips profile blocks <- scripts/membudget run (cmd_run :555-855): ledger-unit refusal, _auto_mb pow2 of max recorded peak (floor 64, ceiling AGDA_MB_MAX), load gate, claim exclusivity, lock-free probe then locked recheck, WAIT-line FIFO, dead-owner gc, systemd-run --user --scope MemoryMax with MemorySwapMax=0 else scripts/cgroup-scope else REFUSE exit 3, sched-batch, /usr/bin/time -v for maxRSS, on 137 or 143 releases and re-execs at double size. LEDGERS: .agda-times.tsv (writer membudget _record_time, success only; readers _auto_mb, buildtime.py, check_cap_ratchet, hook cap ratchet), .agda-profile.tsv (shim via proofcost; not touched by a membudget swap), labels.tsv (writer _record_time; readers membudget peaks, label_lease, gate_status.measure_peaks), .ingested and .promoted stamps (Flat.mk touch; reader reconcile), postgres (sppf_db --ingest-core), the shared budget.cotype (bash and python both). HOOK: Phase 0 census sync; Phase A about 36 gates before the build; build only if fail==0 and skipped when .full-build-stamp is under 7 days old unless a structural change forces it; gen_catalog then git add; Phase C after the build (Set1 ratchet reads .agdai cores, cap ratchet reads .agda-times.tsv). build_census.py PARSES the text of scripts/membudget and refuses if the lease-default assignment is respelled. | 2026-10-10: 2026-10-10 W324 FINDINGS. CORRECTION OF MY OWN CLAIM: I recorded on W77 and W79 that mikemol-membudget run applies no memory cap (mtools residue R1 as it read at commit b91641e, 2026-09-23). The INSTALLED client (mtools 6c242bba) caps: core.run_once puts the payload in a cgroup-v2 sibling (cgroup.py), and the header at membudget_cli.py:17-24 says so. POSITIVE CONTROL on this host, run with a scratch ledger so the shared one was untouched: mikemol-membudget run 64 w324-hog -- a bounded 200 MiB allocation exited 137 with 'OOM-killed at 64MB ... memory.events oom_kill=1 ... the cap was a ceiling'; a trivial payload ran under MemoryMax=64M. waypoints.title: Differential test of bash and python membudget on one ledger and one OOM: retry trigger, peak column, load gate
waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-10: 2026-10-10 from W324. Things only a differential run can settle, none verified: (1) whether a kill from OUTSIDE the cgroup or a self kill -9 climbs the lease (bash retries on exit 137 or 143 with RETRY_OOM; python reads the cgroup oom_kill counter); (2) whether .agda-times.tsv written by the python client has the same column meaning as bash's (peak = maxRSS via wait4 plus an extra cg_peak_mb column versus /usr/bin/time -v), because _auto_mb and check_cap_ratchet read it; (3) the CPU load gate default (bash 10 x nproc via MEMBUDGET_MAXLOAD, python admit.MAXLOAD not read); (4) whether the shared budget.cotype stays consistent when both clients run at once (the cross-client WAIT-line race was never constructed in substrate, see W77). Positive control already done in W324: python client OOM-kills a 200 MiB allocation at a 64 MiB cap on this host. | 2026-10-10: 2026-10-10 DIFFERENTIAL MEASURED, same bounded payloads under scripts/membudget (bash) and .venv/bin/mikemol-membudget (python, mtools 03749d56 descendant of 6c242bba) on SEPARATE scratch ledgers, 256 MB total each; the shared ledger untouched. (1) NORMAL run (/usr/bin/true at 64): equivalent, exit 0. (2) MEMORY KILL (bounded 200 MiB allocation at a 64 MiB cap): bash exits 143 and prints only the shell's 'Terminated'; python exits 137 with the diagnostic 'OOM-killed at 64MB ... memory.events oom_kill=1 ... the cap was a ceiling'. Both codes are in bash's retry set. (3) RETRY LADDER with MEMBUDGET_RETRY_OOM=1 on that real OOM: identical, 64 to 128 to 256 then success. (4) SELF kill -9, NO memory pressure, RETRY_OOM=1: bash MISDIAGNOSES it as OOM and climbs 64, 128, 256, 384 then REFUSES exit 3 'IMPOSSIBLE: need 384MB > 256MB (global total)'; python runs ONCE, exit 137, no climb and no false OOM claim. The oracle listed this as a python regression; measured, it is a python IMPROVEMENT (bash conflates any 137 or 143 with OOM and burns leases). The case python does not climb on is a kill from OUTSIDE the cgroup, where a bigger lease would not help anyway. (5) LEDGER (peaks): same labels and run counts, suggested leases identical (64 and 64, 256 and 256), but PEAK differs for tiny payloads: /usr/bin/true is 1 MB in bash and 13 MB in python (hog 211 vs 212). Likely cause, NOT VERIFIED: ru_maxrss of the child counts the forked python image before exec, a floor of about 12 MB. pow2 bucketing hides it except near a boundary, where python can suggest one bucket higher (a payload truly at 55 MB reads about 67 and leases 128), which only costs packing, never safety. (6) The python client deliberately mirrors bash's env surface (MEMBUDGET_MAXLOAD, NOBLOCK, TIMEOUT, POLL, POLL_MAX, GC_INTERVAL, LOCK_TIMEOUT, RETRY_OOM, MEMBUDGET_LABEL_LEDGER, AGDA_MB_DEFAULT, AGDA_MB_MAX; membudget_cli.py:60-84) and its exit codes (3 impossible, 1 lock, 2 usage). NOT VERIFIED: the load-gate refusal and MAXLOAD's default in python; both clients running at once on ONE ledger (the cross-client WAIT race, never constructed in substrate); a REAL agda compile under the python client and whether the +12 MB floor moves any module's bucket (the .agda-times.tsv peaks run 30 to 200 MB); the python client's 7th column cg_peak_mb. CONCLUSION: enforcement and retry are equal or better in python; the open risks are the peak floor and the unconstructed concurrency case. | 2026-10-10: 2026-10-10: mtools minted mtools:W963 (fence) for the peak floor, and folded into it the two-clients-on-one-ledger harness and the load-gate and MAXLOAD-default checks I could not verify. waypoints.title: tests/test_import_edge_agreement.py imports agda_lex bare and fails when scratch is not on sys.path
waypoints.evidence: 2026-10-10: 2026-10-10 MEASURED: the tool selftests stage died with ModuleNotFoundError: No module named agda_lex at tests/test_import_edge_agreement.py:58 (from agda_lex import agda_files, mask_comments, statements) under the isolated snapshot. The bare name resolves only when scratch or scripts is on sys.path, which the repo's own pyproject gives pytest through pythonpath but not the suite runner. The standing rule is no sys.path edits, so the fix is the dotted import of wherever agda_lex really lives (the module_importers reader flags bare sites as the paydown queue) or a stub-backed package path. Same class as the 13 bare importers module_importers counts elsewhere. | 2026-10-10: 2026-10-10 CORRECTION of this card's own fix shape, learned from W335. The bare spelling of agda_lex and gen_build_makefiles is DELIBERATE, not a bug: tests/test_agda_census_drain.py documents it as a MEASURED constraint (stubs/*.pyi are keyed on the bare module name, so a scripts.-prefixed import bypasses the stub and drags mypy into untyped source, 139 findings on a file that has none). Those bare names resolve only under the pythonpath this project declares for pytest, so the same file fails with ModuleNotFoundError when something RUNS it as a script. So the failure in the 'tool selftests' stage is a PLACEMENT problem: run_selftests discovered tests/test_import_edge_agreement.py as a suite and ran it by path, outside pytest's pythonpath. 'Switch to a dotted import' would be the wrong fix (it re-creates the 139 findings). The honest options: (a) make suite discovery skip tests/ because pytest owns that directory (and check the 'tool unit tests' stage covers them, which W335 just made collect), or (b) give the discovery run the same pythonpath pytest uses. Check which discovery rule admitted the file before deciding. | 2026-10-10: 2026-10-10 ROOT CAUSE FOUND. substrate/suite_discovery.py HANDLES_SELFTEST is a bare regex over the WHOLE source, so the prose sentence in a docstring that says a file cannot be run as --selftest admitted it as a suite. Both tests/test_import_edge_agreement.py and tests/test_agda_census_drain.py are admitted that way, and the full pytest run over tests/ is 68 passed, so pytest already owns them. Fix designed: a code-only flag test (ast: a non-docstring string constant naming the flag; SyntaxError falls back to the regex), expected effect 509 suites to 507. Not landed: suite_discovery.py has 33 per-file findings (its noqa S603/S607 lines), so any edit is refused and it needs the drain method (clean modules plus a one-Write shim, golden before/after on run_selftests --list). | 2026-10-10: 2026-10-10 LANDED (uncommitted, staged for W333): suite_discovery.py drained to a shim over substrate/suite_flag.py (code-only flag test via ast, docstring prose no longer counts) and substrate/suite_walk.py (git-ignore-driven walk, absolute-path git so no suppression). suite_discovery_selftest 10/10, run_selftests_selftest 9/9, full pytest tests 68 passed. run_selftests --list went 509 to 500: the 2 tests/ files left as designed, and 7 more left (bare_speech, flag_ownership, iface_construct, iface_cost, iface_dataflow, iface_readers, stub_top_type), each an implementation module that named selftest only in prose and already has a sibling selftest file, so they were phantom double-counts. standing: Before launching any subagent, read the reviewed-loop skill and resume the warm reviewer; at most one token spender runs at a time.
Minting or queuing a card is never an operator ask: queue it, and ask only through an `operator: decide` or `operator: act` card.

An operator directive that changes the arc mid-tick closes the open tick first: --tick-close naming the card G0 advanced, --blocked-by the directive's card, and --reason quoting the operator uuid. The directive's work then runs as a '-' interrupt or as a new tick with its own G0. Never hold the tick lock across an arc change.

Before any mikemol-commit while the real index holds staged paths the commit does not carry, preserve the index as a ref (git update-ref refs/preserve/<card>-staged-<date> on a commit-tree of git write-tree) and log the sha on the card.

Every tick runs `nemik-check --warnings --repo substrate` in the background right after --tick-open (it left the tick hooks only because it ran >300 s inside the call, a tool defect carded with nemik), and G1 quotes its exit line or says UNOBSERVED with elapsed time; it is never skipped.

Each subagent launch and each return is a ledger '-' line ('spender: <agent> start' / 'return'), and the session makes no other tool calls in between, so the one-token-spender rule is checkable afterwards.
G0 is written in its own call, and --tick-open is issued only after that call returns success; never in the same parallel batch. A refused G0 write means no tick-open.

Card text containing $, backticks or make syntax goes to the writer from a file ("$(cat FILE)"), never inline (double quotes expand it; the shellcheck hook refuses single-quoted $), and the card is re-read with --show after the write to confirm the literal landed.

An --atomize tick writes each child's source pointer (git sha plus the line it came from) into that child's evidence in the same tick. Any field G0 promises is a value or the literal UNKNOWN, never a placeholder title.

A blocker with no card yet is written as text, '<repo>: ask <UTC date> — <what>', and replaced by the card id when it exists. A local card is never a placeholder blocker. Before adding an edge, check its direction: X is blocked on Y only if X cannot proceed until Y is done.

After --tick-close on a non-main branch (gate-rebuild, while its gate is advisory; re-review when mtools:W2581 lands), commit .claude/paths-forward.json, .ledger and .md through mikemol-commit, read its last line, wait for the post-commit marker, and push the branch by name.

A set of rows taken from a log or a tool's output is produced by a tool mode, never a hand filter. If no mode exists, store the log as a git blob, cite its sha, and card the missing mode (summit capability first) before relying on the rows.
